h1: Saku Boutique Homestay — a tiny homestay where the owners cook Thai–French food for you
intro: This isn't a hotel — it's a home that opens its doors to strangers. Saku Boutique Homestay is a small boutique homestay of just 5 rooms in Saraphi, right on the Chiang Mai–Lamphun border. What guests mention again and again are the owners — Saku and Danny — who designed every corner of the house themselves, cook fresh Thai–French meals, and look after guests like visiting friends. There's a garden pool and a quiet terrace. From approx ฿900/night · scored 9.8 on Trip.com.

body.html: Saku Boutique Homestay is a tiny homestay of just 5 rooms in the Saraphi area, sitting right on the line between Chiang Mai and Lamphun. What gets people talking isn't its size or a hotel-style facilities list — it's how genuinely it feels like a home the owners designed and run themselves. Saku and Danny, the couple who own it, did the interiors, planted the garden, and welcome guests in person. Many reviews say it feels more like staying at a friend's house than renting a room.

All 5 rooms are air-conditioned and have a private balcony looking onto the garden. Each has its own name and decor — Twin Bed Garden View, King Bed Garden View, and a Family Room. The rooms are a comfortable size with soft beds and clean bathrooms. It isn't resort-grade luxury, but it's clean and arranged with a care a chain hotel can't match. With only a handful of rooms, guests get real privacy and quiet.
"It felt like staying at a friend's house. The owners are lovely, the food is delicious, the room is clean, the pool is pretty, and it's incredibly peaceful."

The most-praised part is the food. Saku cooks both Thai and French dishes fresh, bakes the bread, and serves a cooked-to-order breakfast from 7:30–10:30 on the garden terrace. Many reviews describe eating breakfast among the flowers with birdsong as the moment they remember most from the trip. On some evenings the owners arrange a special dinner — a BBQ or a Thai spread — if you ask ahead, a charm you won't find at an ordinary hotel.

Beyond the food, there's an outdoor garden pool, a terrace to lounge on, a small bar and a massage service. The owners also help organise local trips and run guests into town at certain times. The overall feel is genuinely quiet and rural — ideal for anyone who wants to escape the bustle and reset. The trade-off is that this isn't the place for a full facilities list or for stepping out the door straight into shops and cafes.

The location is the one thing to understand before booking. Saku sits in rural Saraphi on the Chiang Mai–Lamphun border — a fair drive from both town centers and hard to find without GPS. It's about 25–30 minutes' drive from Chiang Mai Airport. Reviews agree you should drive yourself or rely on the transport the owners arrange, because hailing a car out here is tough. If you plan to be in town every day the distance can be a limitation, but if you're after a quiet base to recharge, this kind of setting becomes a plus.

Straight up: Saku Boutique Homestay isn't for everyone. There are few rooms, it's hard to book in peak season, and the location is far from town. But for those who want a warm, owner-run stay with fresh home cooking and real garden quiet, it delivers a feeling that hotels at the same price simply can't. A 9.8 on Trip.com and 4.7/5 on TripAdvisor from past guests say that people who click with this place tend to leave genuinely charmed.

A tip from reading the reviews: let the owners know ahead if you'd like dinner at the house, and give a clear arrival time — this is a home, not a 24-hour front desk. Pin the GPS location firmly before you set off, and if you're not driving, ask about transport when you book.

faq.q: Where is Saku Boutique Homestay and what's nearby?
faq.a: It's at 106/6 Moo 8 in Saraphi, on the Chiang Mai–Lamphun border · about 20–30 minutes' drive from both Lamphun town and Chiang Mai town · close to Chiang Mai Promenada and Nong Hoi Market, around 15 minutes · roughly 25–30 minutes from Chiang Mai Airport · it's a quiet rural area, so use GPS — the spot is hard to find.

faq.q: What are Saku Boutique Homestay's starting prices and room types?
faq.a: From approx ฿900/night for a Garden View room · the main types are Twin Bed Garden View, King Bed Garden View and a Family Room, all with private garden-view balconies · prices shift by season, so compare a few platforms before booking.

faq.q: Who is Saku Boutique Homestay best for?
faq.a: It's ideal for couples or anyone who wants to recharge in a quiet, home-like setting · focused on fresh home cooking, owner care and privacy · not the pick for a full facilities list or a central in-town location.

faq.q: What is the food like at Saku Boutique Homestay?
faq.a: The owner (Saku) cooks both Thai and French dishes fresh and bakes the bread · breakfast is cooked to order from 7:30–10:30 and served on the garden terrace · on some evenings the owners arrange a special dinner — a BBQ or a Thai spread — if you ask ahead, the most-praised part of the stay.

faq.q: Is it easy to reach Saku Boutique Homestay without a car?
faq.a: Honestly, cars are hard to hail in Saraphi and the location is hard to find · it's best to drive yourself or ask the owners about transfers when you book · pin the GPS firmly before travelling, as it sits deep in a rural area.

faq.q: How well does Saku Boutique Homestay review?
faq.a: It scores 9.8 on Trip.com and 4.7/5 on TripAdvisor from past guests · repeated praise goes to the attentive owners, the food, the clean rooms and the quiet · the main limitations are the out-of-town location and the few rooms.
